title: Rockstar Games Has Honored a Beloved GTA 4 Meme With One of GTA 6's Mechanics
summary: GTA 6 has named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme.

By Cade Onder Updated : Oct 29, 2026 3:25am UTC 5 comments Add IGN on Google GTA 6 has named one of its biggest mechanics after a beloved GTA 4 meme. In 2008, a Justin.tv channel (now known as Twitch) by the name of FourPlayerPodcast made GTA history. One of the hosts of the channel, Brad Simons, rode a moped around GTA 4's Liberty City. He eventually found another moped rider and began comically declaring them "scooter brothers." The video has over 7.5 million views on YouTube , and now it's part of GTA 6. In a new preview from Edge magazine , it was confirmed that players will be able to summon their vehicle using an app called Scooter Brothers. An NPC will deliver your car and then get on a scooter (presumably driven by another "brother") and drive off. Whether or not these so-called scooter brothers will have their own silly lines to honor their origins remains to be seen. GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN View 15 Images In GTA 5, when switching to Trevor, players would have a chance of seeing the wily character recreating the meme with a frightened NPC. It was a pretty great nod, and now, Rockstar is keeping the tradition alive, though this time with more purpose. GTA Online has had a mechanic to let you call your car since launch, and Red Dead Redemption also allows you to summon your horse if it's within a reasonable distance. However, this is the first time players will be able to do something like this without cheats in GTA's single-player. It's arguably more necessary than ever, too, as the player's arsenal of weapons and some other important gear is stored in the trunk of their vehicle. It also means your cars likely won't be as disposable as they were in previous games. All of this news comes just three weeks ahead of GTA 6's launch and two weeks before pre-loading begins. Rockstar's marketing efforts are ramping up across the globe . Rumors also indicate a PC version of the game is just around the corner, with a reported release window of early 2027 . Either way, it's an exciting time to be a GTA fan. Cade Onder Freelance Writer X Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more.
